notes: Read both units, full federal-tribal context, all seven candidates and the review. Replaced every unresolved group attribution with the Republican Party. Split respect for tribal representation from the encouragement to other governments. Restored the state-regulation comparison. Preserved the Democratic Party allegation as the platform's assertion and restored its especially-egregious evaluation rather than presenting it as independently established fact.

claims.claim_text: The Republican Party respects tribal governments as the voices of their communities.
The Republican Party encourages federal, state and local governments to heed tribal governments when developing partnerships and programs to improve life for American Indians and their neighbors.
The Republican Party considers economic self-sufficiency the ultimate answer to challenges confronting Indian country.
The Republican Party considers tribal governments and their communities better situated than Washington bureaucracies to solve systemic poverty and disenfranchisement.
The Republican Party says the federal government should neither burden states with regulations nor stifle resource development on reservations.
Reservations should receive federal assistance for roads and technology that advance their commerce nationally.
Federal and state job-blocking regulations should be withdrawn or redrawn so tribal governments acting for American Indians are not disadvantaged.
The Republican Party calls it especially egregious that, in its account, the Democratic Party persistently undermined tribal sovereignty to benefit union bosses in tribal workplaces.
